reference.title: Dumbbell Pullover
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the dumbbell goes back behind the head, exhale as you pull it back over the chest.
breathing.cadence: About 2.4 s down, 0.4 s stretch, 1.6 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9). Start light: the stretched overhead position limits the load.
prescription.progression: More reps, a 1 s pause in the stretch, then the next dumbbell.

cues.text: Lie along a flat bench with your head near the end, feet planted. Hold one dumbbell over the chest with both palms cupping the top plate, arms nearly straight.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head, elbows staying softly bent, ribs down.
Stop when the arms are about in line with the body and the lats and chest feel a stretch; do not let the low back arch.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbell back along the same arc until it is over the chest.
Pause over the chest with the arms nearly straight, then go again.

mistakes.mistake: Bending and straightening the elbows (turning it into a triceps extension)
mistakes.fix: Keep the same soft elbow bend through the whole arc.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching off the bench at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Brace the abs, keep the ribs down and stop the arc where the back stays flat.
Lower slowly to about arms in line with the body; go deeper only if the shoulders are comfortable.

mistakes.mistake: Loose grip on the dumbbell over the face
mistakes.fix: Cup the top plate firmly with both palms, thumbs around the handle, and use a dumbbell with fixed plates.

mistakes.mistake: Head hanging off the end of the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep the back of the head on the bench and the neck neutral.

kinematics.setup: Along the bench, top of the head at the end of the pad (1.6 cm past it)
kinematics.peak: Glutes, upper back and head on the bench (skinned mesh within about 1 cm, measured with b2/chest_mesh.mjs)
kinematics.norm: Lying along a flat bench, head and hips supported (as in Teixeira 2022, supine on a flat bench); the cross-bench version with only the shoulders on the bench is an alternative (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈172° at the bottom (arms aimed 14° above the line of the back so the dumbbell clears the head and the bench end)
kinematics.norm: From about 90 degrees (arms over the chest) to about 180 degrees (arms in line with the body); Teixeira 2022 tested 0-180 degrees, with pectoralis peaking at 90-135 degrees and latissimus at 135-180 degrees
Nearly straight with a soft, fixed bend (clinical opinion); a bent-arm pullover raised peak activity in most muscles versus the conventional version (Washif 2016)

kinematics.setup: Both palms on the top plate, dumbbell hanging 48.1 cm above the shoulder line at its centre
kinematics.peak: Dumbbell behind the head, lowest point 51.7 cm above the floor, beyond the bench end
kinematics.norm: One dumbbell, both palms cupping the top plate (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 2.4 s down, 0.4 s stretch, 1.6 s up, 0.6 s over the chest
kinematics.norm: Slow and controlled, about 2-3 s down and 1.5-2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Campos and Silva 2014, comparison of electromyographic activity during the bench press and barbell pullover exercises (Motriz 20(2):200-205)

Teixeira, Gomes, da Silva, Magalhães and Marchetti 2022, differences between pullover and pulldown exercises on maximal isometric force and myoelectric activity in recreationally-trained men (Int J Exerc Sci 15(4):797-807; PMC9362894)

Washif, Hébert-Losier and Beaven 2016, electromyographic assessment of pullover exercise variations and javelin throw on nine upper-body muscles (poster, 10th International Conference on Strength Training; University of Waikato Research Commons)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit on the end of the bench with the dumbbells on the thighs, then lie back and kick them up one knee at a time; at the end of the set bring them back to the thighs or lower them to the floor beside the bench rather than dropping them (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain overhead (for example impingement): keep the arc short, stopping with the arms well above the line of the body, or choose another lat or chest exercise (clinical opinion).
Hold the dumbbell firmly over the face; use a fixed-plate dumbbell, never one with loose collars.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Limited overhead mobility: shorten the arc.
Low back arching: put the feet on the end of the bench or bend the knees more.
regressions: Lighter dumbbell with a short arc.
progressions: Slower lowering with a pause in the stretch.
Cross-bench pullover (shoulders on the bench, hips low).

muscleNotes.pec_r: Pulls the arms from behind the head back over the chest (shoulder extension from overhead). Pectoralis activity peaked between about 90 and 135 degrees of shoulder flexion in an isometric pullover (Teixeira 2022), but it was lower than in the bench press (Campos 2014).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Pulls the arms from behind the head back over the chest (shoulder extension from overhead). Pectoralis activity peaked between about 90 and 135 degrees of shoulder flexion in an isometric pullover (Teixeira 2022), but it was lower than in the bench press (Campos 2014).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Shoulder extensor from the overhead position; latissimus activity was higher at 135-180 degrees of flexion than near the chest (Teixeira 2022) and higher in the pullover than the bench press (Campos 2014).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Shoulder extensor from the overhead position; latissimus activity was higher at 135-180 degrees of flexion than near the chest (Teixeira 2022) and higher in the pullover than the bench press (Campos 2014).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: The long head crosses the shoulder and helps extend it; it was more active in the pullover than the bench press (Campos 2014). It also holds the elbows nearly straight.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: The long head crosses the shoulder and helps extend it; it was more active in the pullover than the bench press (Campos 2014). It also holds the elbows nearly straight.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Controls the shoulder blades as they rotate upward overhead and back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Controls the shoulder blades as they rotate upward overhead and back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the dumbbell, both hands cupping the top plate.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the dumbbell, both hands cupping the top plate.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down: the low back should not arch as the arms go overhead.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Steady the shoulder blades on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Steady the shoulder blades on the bench.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help keep the ribs from flaring as the arms reach overhead.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help keep the ribs from flaring as the arms reach overhead.
